title: US government funding expires on 11 December 2026
what_happened: Current federal appropriations run out on 2026-12-11 under Public Law 119-103, during the lame-duck session before the new Congress convenes in January 2027.
how_it_reaches_markets: A lapse in funding would shut parts of the federal government, delay official economic data used by the Fed and markets, and weigh on confidence.

sourced_facts.text: Public Law 119-103 (Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027), enacted 2026-09-02: funds are available until regular appropriations are enacted or 'December 11, 2026', whichever comes first (Sec. 106)
White House, 2026-09-02: the act 'includes a short-term continuing resolution that provides fiscal year 2027 appropriations to Federal agencies through December 11, 2026'

resolved_when_all: A funding law covering the period beyond 2026-12-11 is signed
worsened_when_any: Funding lapses and a shutdown begins
A shutdown lasts more than 14 days

relief_headlines_that_do_not_resolve_it: A short stopgap of under 30 days (the deadline moves, the risk stays open; record the new date in history)
